purpose: Deterministic full-interval catch-up. A process is never considered settled merely because its first overdue boundary or aggregate clock was resolved.
closure_target: exact reached world time or earlier hard player interrupt

player_boundary_semantics.internal_boundary: Scheduler, training, recovery, mission, movement, economy, institution, faction, team, formation, population, or other causal work that changes persistent truth but creates no new player-facing situation. Event-seeking callers continue automatically; this boundary never sets decision_required and never closes time passage by itself.
player_boundary_semantics.soft_player_facing_event: A committed report, mission offer, teammate contact, public consequence, institutional transition, observable pressure, or other player-visible development that merits narration but does not itself require a protected Wei choice. Event-seeking callers stop so ChatGPT can render the scene; decision_required remains null and time passage remains allowed unless a separate hard decision exists. The event-seeking result should expose only a bounded event cue (kind plus already-player-safe stable refs) so the exact relevant owner can be rehydrated without world scanning.
player_boundary_semantics.hard_player_decision: A protected player choice that cannot be lawfully supplied by standing orders, delegation, or deterministic mechanics. Time stops at the exact boundary, time_passage_allowed becomes false, and decision_required identifies the unresolved choice.

event_seeking_rule: Event-seeking downtime is a caller policy over the same temporal settlement path: process one bounded causal boundary, continue automatically across internal-only results, stop softly on the first committed player-facing event, and stop hard on the first protected player decision. It never invents an event to satisfy the request.
procedure_time_rule: A substantive already-established conversation, briefing, examination stage, review, consultation, negotiation, or council may settle durable elapsed time through procedure_time_resolution. The caller supplies the exact fresh scene_id and one closed authored procedure kind, never arbitrary seconds. Static procedure-time policy derives the horizon; event-seeking temporal settlement remains the sole clock authority and may stop earlier at a soft player-facing event or hard protected decision. Procedure-time settlement never creates or decides the procedure's domain outcome.
selection_order: globally earliest unresolved process boundary, owner-local deadline, or causal trigger first; deterministic tie order by stable process/owner id unless a registered dependency overrides it
scheduled_loop: collect all active processes with next_due <= target plus every covered owner whose saved local next_due/deadline <= target plus every causal wake-up created inside the interval
resolve the globally earliest process boundary, owner-local deadline, or causal wake-up from its actual owner/process cursor to that exact time
apply authoritative outputs and wake every causally affected owner even when its aggregate baseline is not due

if an autonomous owner remains active after review, select a lawful next action or persist an explicit no-material-action result; if a plan completes, create or activate a lawful successor immediately
advance only the recurrence or owner-local deadline actually reviewed, to a strictly later due time unless completed/blocked
write the semantic process receipt after all covered work for the reviewed span is resolved
reinsert process, owner deadlines, causal wakes and new successor processes and continue until none are due through target
continuous_residual: After all full boundaries and owner-local wakes, every active unblocked process with accrual_mode=continuous resolves its remaining span through exact target. Its frontier cursor may advance only with a matching state/runtime.json semantic receipt; a slower monthly/weekly next_due does not suppress owner-local or causal review.
new_process_rule: Any process created or activated at time <= target must itself be settled/caught up through target unless completed, paused, blocked, or stopped by player interrupt.
hard_interrupt_rule: Only a protected player choice is a hard interrupt. At that decision, stop at the exact interrupt timestamp and make that the reached world time. Never simulate beyond it. A report, offer, contact, or other player-visible development without a protected choice is a soft event, not a hard interrupt.

recurrence_kinds.calendar_month_start: advance to first day of next calendar month at registered clock
recurrence_kinds.calendar_month_end: advance to last day of next calendar month at registered clock
recurrence_kinds.calendar_quarter_start: advance to first day of next calendar quarter at registered clock
recurrence_kinds.calendar_quarter_end: advance to last day of next calendar quarter at registered clock
recurrence_kinds.calendar_year_start: advance to first day of next calendar year at registered clock; historical calendars have no year zero
recurrence_kinds.one_shot: after resolution process completes or is superseded; no automatic recurrence
recurrence_kinds.triggered: no next_due; resolve whenever registered trigger becomes true

accrual_modes.continuous: all elapsed time counts, including final partial interval
accrual_modes.boundary_only: state changes only on due boundary/trigger; no invented partial-cycle result

postconditions: no covered owner-local next_due/deadline <= world_time remains unresolved
no unresolved triggered condition with trigger_time <= world_time
continuous active unblocked processes settled_through == world_time
every continuous process at world_time has a matching semantic receipt reviewed_through == its frontier cursor with the coverage used for that review
state/runtime.json last_settled_at == world_time only after all required continuous receipts close
every newly activated process caught up through world_time
every evolving owner has process coverage
no elapsed eligible development/resource/recovery time lost
autonomous_action_rule: At every aggregate boundary, owner-local deadline, or causal wake-up, evaluate lawful next actions from current goals, knowledge, authority, resources, location, opposition, and standing orders. Material actions instantiate an operation/mission/event before resolution and remain inside catch-up through the target time. A no-op is valid only after that evaluation is actually performed and receipted.

efficiency_policy.baseline: Distant inactive owners may use coarse monthly/weekly aggregate fallbacks. Saved owner-local deadlines, active plan milestones, mission/deployment clocks, information delivery, combat, assignment, movement, injury, resource thresholds, or player contact wake the affected owner immediately. Compression may reduce review work only when the equivalent semantic result is proven; it may never replace an owner review with aggregate timestamp advancement.
